summary: AI observability gives teams visibility into how LLM applications behave in production, surfacing latency, errors, token usage, cost, and output quality through distributed tracing and evaluation. As LLM apps grow more complex and expensive, observability is essential for debugging multi-step chains, controlling API spend, and ensuring reliable, high-quality responses. Modern 2026 tools emphasize span-level tracing, trace replay for debugging, and research-backed evaluations.

tools.name: LangSmith
tools.monitors: End-to-end traces of LLM chains and agents, latency, token usage, cost, and evaluation metrics, with deep integration into the LangChain ecosystem.
features: Distributed tracing with span hierarchies for chains and agents
Native LangChain/LangGraph integration (framework-agnostic SDK also available)
tools.pricing: Free tier includes 5,000 monthly traces. Beyond the allowance, base traces (14-day retention) cost $2.50 per 1k and extended traces (400-day retention) cost $5.00 per 1k; paid Plus seat-based plans add higher limits and collaboration features.
tools.best_for: Teams building on LangChain/LangGraph that want tightly integrated tracing, evaluation, and prompt management.

tools.name: Helicone
tools.monitors: LLM API requests and responses via a proxy, tracking cost, token usage, latency, caching, and rate limits across providers.
features: One-line proxy integration for request logging
Response caching to cut repeated-call costs
Rate limiting and custom properties for segmentation
tools.pricing: Free tier includes 10,000 monthly traces. Pro plan at $79/month (approx. $79 per 100,000 traces), Team plan at $799/month, and custom enterprise pricing.
tools.best_for: Teams wanting fast, low-effort cost monitoring and caching via a drop-in proxy across multiple LLM providers.

tools.name: Weights & Biases (W&B)
tools.monitors: The full ML and LLM lifecycle, including experiment metrics, model training runs, and (via W&B Weave) LLM traces, evaluations, and production monitoring.
features: W&B Weave for LLM tracing and evaluation
tools.pricing: Free tier for personal/open-source use; usage-based paid Pro plans; custom Enterprise pricing for larger teams and on-prem/VPC deployment.
tools.best_for: ML/AI teams that want unified experiment tracking plus LLM observability in one platform.

tools.name: Arize AI
tools.monitors: Production model and LLM performance, including drift, data quality, embedding/cluster analysis, latency, and evaluation of LLM outputs.
features: LLM tracing and evaluation (via Arize Phoenix, open source)
Drift, data quality, and performance monitoring
Embedding and cluster visualization for root-cause analysis
Online and offline evaluations with LLM-as-judge
tools.pricing: Arize Phoenix is free and open source; Arize AX offers a free tier with paid Pro and custom Enterprise plans for production-scale monitoring.
tools.best_for: Enterprises needing production-grade ML and LLM monitoring with strong drift detection and root-cause analysis.

tools.name: LangFuse
tools.monitors: LLM application traces, spans, token usage, cost, latency, and quality scores, with open-source self-hosting support.
features: Open-source, self-hostable tracing with span hierarchies
tools.pricing: Open-source self-hosted tier is free. Cloud Hobby tier is free with limits; paid Core/Pro and Enterprise plans scale with event volume, retention, and features.
tools.best_for: Teams wanting an open-source, self-hostable observability platform with full data control and flexible pricing.

tools.name: OpenLLMetry
tools.monitors: LLM and vector-database calls through OpenTelemetry-based instrumentation, capturing traces, latency, token usage, and cost in a vendor-neutral way.
features: Auto-instrumentation for popular LLM and vector DB SDKs
Export to any OTel-compatible backend (Traceloop, Datadog, Grafana, etc.)
Standardized semantic conventions for GenAI spans
tools.pricing: Free and open source (Apache-licensed); costs come only from the chosen backend or Traceloop's managed platform, which offers free and paid tiers.
tools.best_for: Teams wanting vendor-neutral, standards-based instrumentation that plugs into existing observability stacks.

cost_tips: Cache responses for repeated or similar prompts (e.g., via Helicone or a semantic cache) to avoid paying for identical LLM calls.
Route requests to the smallest model that meets quality needs and reserve large frontier models for complex tasks; use prompt-based routing or tiered fallbacks.
Trim token usage by shortening prompts, compressing context, limiting retrieved RAG chunks, and capping max output tokens.
Monitor cost per user, feature, and model with observability dashboards to catch runaway spend, then set budgets, rate limits, and alerts.
